text:
simon: FYI I saw a p99 tail spike (~2.1s -> 4.8s) on streaming chat after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. reproducing on canary with microbatch=8.
maya: ugh. Is it only streaming? non-streaming completions fine?
pranav: non-streaming completions (batching flush) stayed within p99 1.2s, so seems streaming path impacted.
elaine: any quick profile data? flamegraphs or timeline?
simon: pasted a tiny profile snippet from the canary run:```
[PROFILE] timeline: request 0 -> enqueue(5ms) -> select-kernel(12ms) -> kv-lookup(30ms) -> microbatch-assemble(45ms) -> attention-kernel(220ms) -> stream-serialize(120ms) -> epilogue-copy(200ms)
p95 420ms p99 4800ms (tail dominated by epilogue-copy + stream-serialize)
```
maya: epilogue-copy jumping to 200ms for a subset of requests is suspicious — could be cacheline contention or memcpy path hitting fallback path.
pranav: kernel-selector changed to prefer fused-attention on sequences < 128, else generic. Might cause different memory layout or KV state shapes for small streaming tokens.
elaine: also remember streaming keeps KV warm across microbatches; non-streaming evicts between requests. KV cache behavior can expose hot-path locking when a lot of microbatches try to append.
simon: agree. I did a trace: when microbatch size > 6 we see more concurrent KV appends per GPU which bumps a spinlock in kv-store.c. trace excerpt:```
KV_APPEND lock-hold: 0.1ms typical, 5-15ms in tail cases
contending threads: 3-7
```
maya: so microbatch sizing is a lever: smaller microbatches reduce contention but increase scheduling overhead and hurt throughput.
pranav: for streaming chat we want low p99/p95; suggest dynamic cap: microbatch cap = min( floor(target_latency / avg_token_time), global_max) with different target_latency for streaming vs completions.
elaine: we tried dynamic cap last quarter; it helped until load hit 300 rps and then throughput collapsed because scheduler thrashing. we need a hysteresis + steady-state estimator.
simon: thought: add an early-flush path for streaming when partial-latency exceeds threshold. basically, if first token of microbatch has waited > x ms, force flush that microbatch even if not full. reduces tail for chat.
maya: that's similar to the head-flush idea we discussed. It's good for interactive sessions; for completions where we prefer throughput, keep full microbatching.
pranav: kernel selection angle: switch to a KV-friendly kernel (less memcpy) for streaming microbatches. We can mark kernels with attributes: {kv_friendly: true}. Scheduler chooses kv_friendly when streaming flag true.
elaine: we'll need to measure cost: kv_friendly kernels increase per-token latency by ~5% but drop kv-append contention by 60% in synthetic. can we accept 5% baseline bump for better tail?
maya: tradeoff: latency SLO is p99 < 500ms for interactive tier. If kv_friendly keeps p99 <= 500ms under load, 5% median raise is OK. For batch completions SLO is throughput per GPU. So use different kernel routing.
runtime-oncall: note: ensure we don't regress cold-start throughput. tagging kernels must preserve fallback to default during shortages.
pranav: quick experiment plan:
- run mixed workload (60% streaming chat, 40% completions) on canary pool
- variants: microbatch cap {4,8,12}, early-flush enabled/disabled, kernel routing {default, kv_friendly}
- collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, kernel-switch counts, kv-lock-hold histogram
simon: I already ran a small sweep overnight. short summary:
- cap=4 + kv_friendly + early-flush -> p99=480ms, tokens/s -8%
- cap=12 + default kernel + no early-flush -> p99=3.8s, tokens/s +14%
- cap=8 + default + early-flush -> p99=920ms, tokens/s +2%
- cap=8 + kv_friendly + early-flush -> p99=510ms, tokens/s -1%
maya: that suggests 8+kv_friendly+early-flush is the sweet spot for mixed loads.
elaine: can we add a microbenchmark to isolate memcpy path? e.g., run synthetic KV append hot loop and measure memcpy fallback threshold.
simon: done: memcpy fallback triggers when buffer size > 2MB or alignment not 64B. Our streaming microbatch assembly sometimes produces unaligned fragments after tokenization.
pranav: small change: enforce 64B alignment in microbatch assembly for streaming path. Should reduce fallback occurrences. cheap patch.
maya: good. Also let's add a p99 guard in scheduler: if observed p99 > target, reduce cap by 2 and enable early-flush automatically per pool.
elaine: put metrics: pool.runtime.microbatch.cap, pool.runtime.early_flush.enabled, pool.runtime.kernel_hint. We'll need dashboard panels and alert if p99 > 2x target.
runtime-oncall: reminded: rollouts should be canary then blue-green with 5% increments. set revert-on-p99-regression flag.
simon: I'll open the PR: changes are (1) kernel attribute & routing, (2) early-flush path, (3) 64B alignment in assembler, (4) scheduler p99-based cap adjuster.
pranav: rough estimate of perf impact: tokens/s -~1-3% on average, p99 improvement ~4-8x in heavy contention scenarios.
maya: ok let's run the 4-way sweep on canary tonight and get flamegraphs for both cases. If stable, we ship to 10% tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: scheduled job run "microbatch-sweep-canary-176823" started (canary pool 3 nodes)
elaine: thanks. keep thread updated with results. small follow-ups: add unit test for assembler alignment and a stress test for kv append lock.
simon: will do. thanks all.
